cards.name: CC Glass Wipe
cards.summary: Wipes the layer away through a refractive, melting-glass edge: a gradient layer's luminance decides which areas go first, and the edge displaces the image like liquid glass while the reveal layer shows through. Needs a Layer to Reveal (and ideally a textured Gradient Layer) set by script: both default to the clip itself, so a spec-only apply wipes nothing and only smears the picture slightly along the glassy edge.
use_for: dreamy / flashback transition in a documentary
liquid reveal of a title card or logo bumper
soft organic scene change in an AI-education explainer
water / heat themed transition in a trailer
avoid: spec-only apply with Layer to Reveal left at its default (the clip itself): nothing wipes away, the frame only warps slightly even at Displacement 300 / Softness 80 (verified); set Layer to Reveal to the incoming clip or 0 (None) by script
with no textured Gradient Layer the wipe follows the clip's own luminance and can look blotchy
large Displacement Amount smears faces mid-transition; keep it short on interview shots

params.name: Completion
params.does: transition progress in % (0 = untouched, 100 = fully revealed)

params.name: Layer to Reveal
params.does: layer shown where the wipe has passed; default is the effect's own layer, so set it to the incoming clip (or None) by script
params.typical: the incoming clip below this layer

params.name: Gradient Layer
params.does: layer whose luminance sets the order in which areas melt away (default: the effect's own layer)
params.typical: a Fractal Noise or Gradient Ramp precomp, hidden

params.name: Softness
params.does: width of the soft glassy edge

params.name: Displacement Amount
params.does: strength of the refractive distortion along the edge

cards.equivalent: Gradient Wipe video effect (luma-ordered wipe, no refraction); the Glass or Liquid Distortion transition for a refractive feel
cards.scripting: Layer to Reveal and Gradient Layer are layer-reference params (cannot be set from a spec; a script must setValue(layerIndex), 0 = None). Their harvested default is 1 = the effect's own layer, so a spec-only apply reveals the layer's own unaffected source: the visible result is only the glassy distortion band along the edge, and at Completion 100 the frame looks unchanged. Set Layer to Reveal to the incoming clip's index (or 0 to wipe to transparency over a lower layer). Completion is 0-100 raw here. Which luminance end melts first is not verified.

verified.note: Still no wipe: Displacement 300 / Softness 80 only bends the frame slightly more than the old render (the upper-left figure, the left side and block edges smeared, mean change vs old about 7/255) and the old render's bright glassy blobs are gone, because Layer to Reveal defaults to the clip itself so the wiped area shows the same picture; no in-range value fixes that, so the card is set to needs_input (a Layer to Reveal set by script).

cards.name: CC Grid Wipe
cards.summary: Wipes the layer out through a grid of tiles that each open with a radial, door or rectangular pattern, revealing what is underneath.
use_for: energetic scene change in a social reel
reveal of a data card or headline in a news package
rotated diamond-grid wipe for a stylised explainer section break
avoid: reads as a dated broadcast DVE if used repeatedly
very few tiles with no rotation looks like a cheap checkerboard

params.name: Completion
params.does: transition progress, raw 0-1 (UI shows 0-100 %)

params.name: Center
params.does: origin of the grid in comp pixels

params.name: Rotation
params.does: angle of the grid in degrees

params.name: Border
params.does: unverified: believed to set how wide/staggered the band of partially-opened tiles is (harvested range 30-200, default 75)

params.name: Tiles
params.does: number of tiles across the frame

params.name: Shape
params.does: how each tile opens (popup, see enum_labels)

params.name: Reverse Transition
params.does: checkbox: 1 inverts the wipe direction

cards.scripting: Completion's harvested range is 0-1 (fractional), unlike CC Glass Wipe's 0-100; values above 1 clamp to fully wiped. Shape is a 1-based popup (1 Doors, 2 Radial (default), 3 Rectangular (read from After Effects 26.0)). Border's exact meaning is not verified. Reverse Transition is a 0/1 checkbox. Wipes to transparency: the incoming clip must sit on a layer below.

verified.note: The image survives only inside a 45-degree diamond grid of tiles on black, tiles shrinking toward the centre: a clear tiled grid wipe.

cards.name: CC Image Wipe
cards.summary: Wipes the layer away in an order driven by a chosen channel (luminance, colour, alpha...) of a gradient layer, with a soft edge, like a configurable Gradient Wipe.
use_for: ink-bleed or brush-texture transition using a texture precomp as the gradient
luminance-ordered dissolve between two documentary shots
reveal of a map or graphic following its own brightness
avoid: using the clip itself as the gradient gives an unpredictable blotchy wipe
hard edge (Border Softness 0) on noisy footage looks aliased

params.name: Completion
params.does: transition progress, raw 0-1

params.name: Border Softness
params.does: softness of the wipe edge, raw 0-1

params.name: Auto Softness
params.does: checkbox: 1 lets the effect set the edge softness automatically (exact behaviour unverified)

params.name: Layer
params.does: the gradient layer whose channel sets wipe order

params.name: Property
params.does: which channel of the gradient layer orders the wipe (1-based popup, see enum_labels)
params.typical: 5 Luminance (default) or 4 Alpha for a shaped matte

params.name: Blur
params.does: blurs the gradient before use to smooth the wipe

params.name: Inverse Gradient
params.does: checkbox: 1 reverses the wipe order

cards.scripting: Layer (under the Gradient header) is a layer-reference param: set it by layer index in script, not from a spec; harvested default 1 = the effect's own layer, so it wipes in the order of its own luminance. Completion and Border Softness are raw 0-1. Property labels were read from CycoreFXHD/ImageWipe.aex (Red|Green|Blue|Alpha|Luminance|Lightness|Hue|Saturation), exact. Address props by plain name ('Property', 'Blur'): Gradient is a flat header row, not a group.

verified.note: Now a clear luminance-ordered wipe: at Completion 0.7 (was 0.5) about 55% of the frame (dark clothing, faces, hair, red stripes, block fronts, plant) has gone to black with soft blurred edges and only the bright wall, white stripes, block tops and flower highlights remain, where the old render dropped only the darkest areas (about 19%) and read as crushed blacks.

cards.name: CC Jaws
cards.summary: Splits the layer along a line into two halves with toothed, jagged edges that pull apart like opening jaws, revealing what is behind.
use_for: satirical / meme-style transition in a political roast reel
torn-apart reveal for a 'breaking' headline
playful split between before/after shots
avoid: looks cartoonish; wrong tone for serious news or documentary
low Height (default 0.1) gives shallow teeth that read as a plain split; use 0.25+ for visible jaws

params.name: Completion
params.does: how far the jaws have opened, raw 0-1

params.name: Center
params.does: point the split line passes through

params.name: Direction
params.does: angle of the split line in degrees

params.name: Height
params.does: depth of the teeth, raw 0-1

params.name: Width
params.does: number/width of teeth along the edge

params.name: Shape
params.does: tooth shape (popup, see enum_labels)

cards.equivalent: Split transition (approximate: straight break, no teeth)
cards.scripting: Completion and Height are raw 0-1. Shape is a 1-based popup (labels Spikes|RoboJaw|Block|Waves read from CycoreFXHD/Jaws.aex, exact). Reveals transparency, so put the incoming clip on a lower layer.

verified.note: The frame is split horizontally by a black gap edged with interlocking triangular teeth top and bottom: clear jagged jaws opening.

cards.name: CC Light Wipe
cards.summary: Wipes the layer away from a centre point in a round, square or door shape while flooding the remaining image with the light colour, so the picture burns toward white as the hole grows, like a burst of light eating the frame.
use_for: flash-burst transition into a trailer title
glowing iris reveal of a logo or channel bumper
'light at the end' moment in a documentary chapter change
avoid: Intensity is not edge-only: 180 at 40% Completion bleached the whole remaining image to flat white with no detail; keep 40-100 unless a full white flash is the point, and tint it or use Color from Source
overuse makes an edit feel like a 2000s wedding video

params.name: Completion
params.does: transition progress in % (0-100)

params.name: Center
params.does: origin of the light wipe
params.typical: [960, 540] or a light source in the shot

params.name: Intensity
params.does: brightness of the light glow, which spreads outward from the wipe edge over the whole remaining layer (only the far corners kept faint detail at 180); not edge-only
params.typical: 40-100 (higher only for a deliberate white flash)

params.name: Shape
params.does: wipe shape (popup, see enum_labels)

params.name: Direction
params.does: angle of the shape (matters for Doors / Square)

params.name: Color from Source
params.does: checkbox: 1 tints the glow from the image colours

params.name: Color
params.does: colour of the light when Color from Source is 0; at high Intensity it clips to white (#FFE6B0 at 180 rendered neutral ~252 white)

cards.scripting: Completion is 0-100 raw here. Shape is a 1-based popup (labels Doors|Round|Square read from CycoreFXHD/LightWipe.aex, exact; default 2 Round). Reverse Transition and Color from Source are 0/1 checkboxes. Wipes to transparency: incoming clip goes on the layer below.

verified.note: Round black hole in the centre with the remaining image burned toward warm white but still readable (stripes, a small round motif, foreground blocks and plant visible, brightest near the hole at about 252, lower corners about 205), where the old Intensity 180 render bleached everything outside the hole to flat white; Intensity 60 shows the light burn falling off from the wipe edge.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: frame confirms the 180 white-out, but the far corners kept faint detail, so the glow falls off from the wipe edge rather than being a flat fill; Intensity and Color param text reworded (Color no longer says 'light edge'); demo Intensity 60 kept

cards.name: CC Line Sweep
cards.summary: Wipes the layer off along one sweeping staircase edge: right-angled steps whose long faces lie square to the Direction angle and whose short faces are Thickness px tall, the whole staircase tilted a little off the Direction line by Slant. Reads as one stepped diagonal wipe, not a set of stripes.
use_for: fast stylised scene change in a news or sports reel
diagonal reveal of a lower-third or name card
rhythmic beat-cut transition in a social edit
avoid: a small Thickness gives many tiny steps that alias and flicker after compression
dated broadcast look if slow

params.name: Completion
params.does: transition progress in % (0-100)

params.name: Direction
params.does: sweep angle in degrees; 135 wipes from upper-left toward lower-right, and the long step faces lie perpendicular to this angle

params.name: Thickness
params.does: height of each step's short face in pixels (measured ~100 px at 100); at Slant 50 each long face is about 5x as long, so smaller = more, finer steps

params.name: Slant
params.does: how far the staircase as a whole is tilted off the Direction line (long-face length per step); at 50 the steps are right-angled, long faces about 5x Thickness, overall edge about 11 degrees off the Direction line; the 0-99 mapping is unverified

params.name: Flip Direction
params.does: checkbox: 1 reverses the sweep

cards.equivalent: Linear Wipe (approximate: straight edge without the steps)
cards.scripting: Match name is 'CS LineSweep' (not 'CC ...'); always apply by that match name. Completion is 0-100 raw. Wipes to transparency.

verified.note: One diagonal wipe to black whose edge is a staircase of right-angled steps, as the corrected summary says.
verified.recheck: 2026-10-13: re-rendered in live wave 1 (frames the old verdict was judged on: pve/work/gallery_pre_fix/)

previous.why: the verify step rewrote the card text from this render (its rule for 'wrong'); the rewritten card has not been rendered again
re-rendered with the corrected text and values (live wave 1); the new frame matches the corrected card
previous.second_opinion: corrected: verdict and rewrite agreed, but measuring 217.png shows right-angled steps (short face ~100 px = Thickness, long face ~525 px, edge ~11 deg off the 135 line), so Slant does not make 'square vs saw-tooth' steps and Thickness is not the step length along the edge; summary, Direction, Thickness and Slant text corrected; demo_settings unchanged

cards.name: CC Radial ScaleWipe
cards.summary: Opens a circular hole from a centre point and pushes the image outward around it with a radial stretch, so the frame looks sucked outward as the hole grows.
use_for: warp-out transition into a new topic in an explainer
portal-style reveal of a title or logo
punchy zoom-style cut in a social reel
avoid: the stretched pixels smear faces badly; centre the hole away from people
slow use looks cheap; keep it under ~0.6 s

params.name: Completion
params.does: transition progress, raw 0-1

params.name: Center
params.does: centre of the expanding hole in comp pixels
params.typical: [960, 540] or on the subject of the next shot

params.name: Reverse Transition
params.does: checkbox: 1 closes in instead of opening out

cards.scripting: Completion is raw 0-1. The hole reveals transparency; the incoming clip goes on a lower layer.

verified.note: A black circular hole in the centre with the image stretched radially outward around its rim (stripes and foreground blocks smeared into a ring).

cards.name: CC Scale Wipe
cards.summary: Stretches the image from a centre point in a chosen direction, smearing its pixels across the frame like a scan-line stretch; animating Stretch makes a smear-in/smear-out transition.
use_for: smear-in of a title or graphic in a reel
speed-streak transition between shots
glitchy stretch accent on a beat
avoid: no Completion control: the transition is the Stretch keyframes
large stretch on faces looks ugly; use on graphics or wide shots

params.name: Stretch
params.does: amount of stretch (-100..100), sign flips the side that stretches

params.name: Center
params.does: line/point where the stretch starts

params.name: Direction
params.does: angle of the stretch in degrees

cards.scripting: Exact Stretch/Direction semantics are not verified (low confidence): check a rendered frame. There is no Completion property; animate Stretch. Default Direction is 50 degrees.

verified.note: Everything right of the centre line is smeared into horizontal streaks while the left half stays intact: a clear directional pixel stretch.

cards.name: CC Twister
cards.summary: Twists the layer around an axis like a ribbon or page being wrung, with shading, so it flips over to reveal its backside layer.
use_for: flip from one photo/document to another in an explainer
twisting reveal of a quote card or headline
playful transition in a reel
avoid: looks dated if slow; keep it fast
without a Backside layer the reverse shows the same image

params.name: Completion
params.does: how far the twist has travelled, raw 0-1

params.name: Backside
params.does: layer shown on the back of the twisted surface

params.name: Shading
params.does: checkbox: 1 adds light/dark shading for a 3D feel

params.name: Center
params.does: centre of the twist

params.name: Axis
params.does: angle of the twist axis in degrees

cards.equivalent: none in Premiere; Flip Motion transition is the nearest (whole-frame 3D flip, no twist)
cards.scripting: Backside is a layer-reference param: set it by layer index in script (not from a spec). Its harvested default is 1 = the effect's own layer, so a spec-only apply twists back to the same image; point it at the incoming shot for a real transition. Completion is raw 0-1. Shading is a 0/1 checkbox.

verified.note: The image is wrung into a ribbon pinched at the centre and turned along a diagonal axis with black around it: a clear 3D twist.

cards.name: CC WarpoMatic
cards.summary: Warps and dissolves the layer into a reveal layer, with the warp and blend order driven by image brightness or contrast, giving a liquid morph-like transition.
use_for: dream / memory transition in a documentary
morph-like blend between two portraits
trippy transition in a music or trend reel
avoid: high Warp Amount on faces looks grotesque
overused it reads as a cheap effect; use once per piece

params.name: Completion
params.does: transition progress in % (0-100)

params.name: Layer to Reveal
params.does: the incoming layer it warps into

params.name: Reactor
params.does: what orders the warp/blend: the image's brightness, or differences between the two layers (popup, see enum_labels)

params.name: Smoothness
params.does: smoothness of the warp map

params.name: Warp Amount
params.does: strength and sign of the displacement

params.name: Warp Direction
params.does: how the two layers warp relative to each other (popup, see enum_labels)
params.typical: 1 Joint (default) or 2 Opposing for a stronger morph

params.name: Blend Span
params.does: how wide the cross-blend band is

cards.equivalent: Liquid Distortion or Wave transition (approximate warp-dissolve)
cards.scripting: Layer to Reveal is a layer-reference param (set by index in script, not from a spec); its harvested default is 1 = the effect's own layer, so a spec-only apply warps the clip into itself (the warp shows mid-transition, the end frame looks unchanged). Completion is 0-100 raw. Popup labels were read from CycoreFXHD/WarpoMatic.aex (exact): Reactor Brightness|Contrast Differences|Brightness Differences|Local Differences, Warp Direction Joint|Opposing|Twisting.

verified.note: The whole frame melts into liquid, chrome-edged warps that follow image contrast (stripes, faces, foreground blocks): a clear liquid morph.

cards.name: Card Wipe
cards.summary: Breaks the layer into a grid of 3D cards that flip over in sequence to show a back layer, with its own camera, lighting and position/rotation jitter.
use_for: flip a wall of tiles from one photo to the next in a news package
card-flip reveal of a leader portrait or headline card
jittered tiles scattering for a trailer title
photo-mosaic style chapter break in a documentary
avoid: default Transition Completion is 25, so it breaks the frame as soon as it is applied
many rows/columns render slowly; very small cards alias
default lighting is flat; without Specular it can look plastic

params.name: Transition Completion
params.does: how far the flip has travelled across the grid (0-100)

params.name: Transition Width
params.does: how many cards are mid-flip at once (0-100)

params.name: Back Layer
params.does: layer shown on the back of the cards
params.typical: the incoming shot (set by layer index)

params.name: Rows
params.does: number of card rows

params.name: Columns
params.does: number of card columns

params.name: Flip Axis
params.does: axis the cards flip around (popup)

params.name: Flip Order
params.does: sweep order of flips (popup), 9 = Gradient uses Gradient Layer

params.name: Timing Randomness
params.does: randomises each card's start time (0-1)

cards.equivalent: none for per-card flips; nearest are Flip Motion (whole-frame 3D flip) or Checker Wipe / Random Blocks (tiled reveal, no 3D)
cards.scripting: Back Layer and Gradient Layer are layer-reference params (set by layer index in script, not from a spec); harvested default 1 = the effect's own layer, so unset, the card backs show the layer itself. Set Transition Completion explicitly (default 25). 'Focal Length' exists twice: a spec key 'Focal Length' reaches only the first (Camera Position section). The applier has no '#2' syntax and Camera Position / Corner Pins are flat header rows, not groups, so the Corner Pins one is reachable only by its match name 'APC CardWipeCam-0054' in a script. 'Upper Left  Corner' and 'Lower Left  Corner' contain a double space. Camera System 3 needs a comp camera; 2 uses the Corner Pins section. Light Type 3 needs a light layer. Rows & Columns 2 makes Columns follow Rows. Popup labels were read from Card Wipe.aex string tables (Light Type order Point Source, Distant Source, First Comp Light; harvested default 2 = Distant Source).

verified.note: The frame is broken into a 6 x 10 grid of cards caught mid-flip on the vertical axis with black gaps: a clear 3D card-flip wipe.

cards.name: Gradient Wipe
cards.summary: Wipes the layer away in the order of a gradient layer's luminance (dark pixels disappear first), with optional soft edge: the classic luma-matte transition.
use_for: ink / paint / smoke texture transitions using a texture clip as the gradient
soft directional reveal using a Gradient Ramp precomp
documentary chapter change with a burn or paper texture
reveal of a map or infographic
avoid: using the clip itself as gradient gives a random blotchy wipe
Transition Softness 0 on detailed gradients looks noisy and aliased

params.name: Transition Completion
params.does: wipe progress; harvested raw range 0-1 (UI shows %)

params.name: Transition Softness
params.does: edge softness, raw 0-1

params.name: Gradient Layer
params.does: layer whose luminance orders the wipe
params.typical: a hidden texture or Gradient Ramp / Fractal Noise precomp

params.name: Gradient Placement
params.does: how the gradient layer is fitted (popup)

params.name: Invert Gradient
params.does: checkbox: 1 makes light pixels go first

cards.scripting: Gradient Layer is a layer-reference param: set it by layer index in script (not from a spec); by default it uses the effect's own layer. The harvested range for Transition Completion and Transition Softness is raw 0-1 (UI shows %), while sibling Linear Wipe is 0-100; values above 1 clamp, so keep to 0-1. Gradient Placement labels Tile Gradient|Center Gradient|Stretch Gradient to Fit read from Gradient_Wipe.aex (exact). The gradient layer is read without its effects/masks unless it is a precomp.

verified.note: Now a clear luma wipe in progress: at Transition Completion 0.7 (was 0.5) about 56% of the frame (dark clothing, faces, red stripes, block fronts, plant) has wiped to black with soft edges, dark areas first, leaving the bright wall, white stripes and block tops, where the old render removed only the darkest areas (about 27%) and read as crushed blacks.
